# Qovery

> Qovery is an Agentic DevOps platform. It deploys and runs applications, databases, jobs and Helm charts on Kubernetes clusters in your own cloud account (AWS, GCP, Azure, Scaleway) or on your own Kubernetes cluster. People use the Console; scripts and coding agents use the CLI, the REST API, the Terraform provider, the MCP server and the agent skills.

## Start here (for coding agents)

1. Install the agent skills, which plan and run deployments for you: `curl -fsSL https://skill.qovery.com/install.sh | bash`. See [Deploy with AI Agent](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/ai-agent.md).
2. Without the skills, follow [Deploy from a Repository with the CLI and API](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/cli-and-api.md). It covers the whole path as commands:
   - `curl -s https://get.qovery.com | bash` then `qovery auth --headless` (a person approves the sign-in link once)
   - create the project, environment and application with `qovery api "PATH" --method POST`
   - `qovery application deploy --organization "$ORG_NAME" --project PROJECT --environment ENVIRONMENT --application APP --commit-id latest --watch`
3. To read status and logs from an agent, connect the [MCP server](https://www.qovery.com/docs/copilot/mcp-server.md) at `https://mcp.qovery.com/mcp`.
4. To limit what an agent can do, use an [API Policy Token](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/api-policy-token.md). See [Let a Coding Agent Deploy Without Cloud Admin Credentials](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/coding-agent-deploy-access.md).
5. API schema: [OpenAPI file](https://www.qovery.com/docs/api-reference/openapi.yaml), also printed by `qovery api spec`.

## These do not exist

- No repository manifest: `qovery.yml`, `.qovery.yml` and `.qovery.toml` are not read. Do not create them.
- No `qovery init`, no top-level `qovery deploy`, no `qovery token create`.
- No `qovery application create`, `qovery database create`, `qovery project create` or `qovery environment create`. Use `qovery api ... --method POST` or Terraform. `qovery container create` exists for image-based services.
- `qovery context set` takes no flags and is interactive. In scripts, pass `--organization`, `--project` and `--environment` to each command.

## Documentation

### Getting Started

#### Get Started

- [Introduction](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/introduction.md): The Kubernetes control plane for humans and AI agents, on your own infrastructure, cloud or on-premise.
- [Get Started with Qovery](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Choose how to start with Qovery: deploy with an AI agent, migrate an app, set up preview environments, try it locally or connect your own cluster.
- [Deploy with AI Agent](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/ai-agent.md): Tell your AI coding agent to deploy. It handles everything, from your code to a live Kubernetes deployment.
- [Deploy from a Repository with the CLI and API](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/cli-and-api.md): Go from a Git repository to a running app on your cluster using only the Qovery CLI and API, with no Console step. Written for scripts and coding agents.
- [How Qovery Works](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/how-it-works.md): The architecture behind Qovery, an Agentic DevOps platform for humans and AI agents that runs in your own cloud account or on your own Kubernetes cluster.
- [Core Concepts](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/basic-concepts.md): Essential Qovery terminology - Organizations, Clusters, Projects, Environments, Services, and Deployments

##### Installation

- [Test & Learn Locally](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/docker.md): Install Qovery locally for demonstration and testing purposes

###### Managed Cluster

- [Create Your Cluster](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/cloud.md): Set up a managed Kubernetes cluster as the foundation for your Qovery deployment
- [Install Qovery on AWS](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/installation/aws.md): Create your first Kubernetes cluster on AWS in under 30 minutes
- [Install Qovery on GCP](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/installation/gcp.md): Complete guide to installing Qovery on Google Cloud Platform with GKE Autopilot
- [Install Qovery on Azure](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/installation/azure.md): Complete guide to installing Qovery on Microsoft Azure with AKS
- [Install Qovery on Scaleway](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/installation/scaleway.md): Complete guide to installing Qovery on Scaleway with Kapsule Kubernetes
- [BYOK (Bring Your Own Kubernetes)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/installation/kubernetes.md): Connect a Kubernetes cluster you already run: EKS, GKE and Scaleway Kapsule with the Qovery Operator, and any other cluster with the Qovery CLI.

#### Platform Capabilities

##### Core Products

- [Provision](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/qovery-101/provision.md): Provision Kubernetes clusters with networking, IAM and storage on AWS, GCP, Azure or Scaleway, or connect a Kubernetes cluster you already run.
- [Deploy](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/qovery-101/deploy.md): Deploy applications, containers and Helm charts to Kubernetes with Qovery, with auto-deploy from Git, rolling updates, health checks and rollbacks.
- [Observe](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/qovery-101/observe.md): Monitor your applications with built-in observability
- [Optimize](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/qovery-101/optimize.md): Optimize resources and reduce costs with Qovery
- [Secure](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/qovery-101/secure.md): Control access with roles, store secrets as environment variables, sync secrets from Doppler, and track every change in your organization with audit logs.
- [Agent Tasks](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/agent-tasks.md): Deploy AI agents directly on your own infrastructure

##### Security & Compliance

- [Security Overview](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/overview.md): How Qovery keeps your application data in your own cloud account, with encryption, backups, access control, audit logs and incident response.

###### IAM Permissions Reference

- [AWS IAM Permissions Reference](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/aws-iam-permissions.md): Detailed breakdown of every AWS IAM permission required by Qovery and why it's needed
- [GCP IAM Permissions Reference](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/gcp-iam-permissions.md): Detailed breakdown of every GCP IAM permission required by Qovery and why it's needed
- [Azure IAM Permissions Reference](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/azure-iam-permissions.md): Detailed breakdown of every Azure permission required by Qovery and why it's needed
- [Scaleway IAM Permissions Reference](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/scaleway-iam-permissions.md): Detailed breakdown of every Scaleway IAM permission required by Qovery and why it's needed
- [Audit Logs](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/audit-logs.md): Track all actions and changes in your Qovery organization
- [SOC2](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/soc2.md): Cluster advanced settings to apply for SOC 2, such as CloudWatch log retention, VPC flow logs, database and Kubernetes API access, and image retention.
- [GDPR](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/gdpr.md): How Qovery handles personal data under GDPR: data protection by design, the Data Protection Officer, consent, individual rights and data retention.
- [DORA Compliance](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/dora.md): Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) readiness with Qovery
- [HIPAA Compliance](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/security-and-compliance/hipaa.md): HIPAA eligibility and protected health information (PHI) handling with Qovery
- [Maintenance](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/configuration/maintenance.md): Understand how Qovery handles platform maintenance and updates

#### How-to Guides

- [Production Environment Management](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/production-environment-management.md): Set up a production environment on a production cluster: application and database settings, secrets, access control, monitoring and a final checklist.
- [Migrate to Kubernetes](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/cloud-migration-and-scaling.md): Leave the PaaS, keep the workflow. Migrate from Heroku, Render, or Railway to Kubernetes on your own cloud, fully automated by AI
- [Let a Coding Agent Deploy Without Cloud Admin Credentials](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/coding-agent-deploy-access.md): Give Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent the ability to deploy, check logs, and create preview environments on your own AWS, GCP, Azure, or Kubernetes, with a scoped token instead of cloud admin access.

##### Ephemeral Environments

- [Ephemeral Environments](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/ephemeral-environment.md): Create on-demand temporary environments for development, testing, and E2E testing with automated CI/CD workflows
- [Set Up Preview Environments for Every Pull Request](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/preview-environments.md): Create a full-stack preview environment (services, databases, configuration) for every pull request on your own Kubernetes cluster, such as EKS, and delete it when the pull request is merged or closed.
- [Build E2E Testing Ephemeral Environments with GitHub Actions and Qovery](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/use-cases/e2e-testing.md): Step-by-step guide to build e2e testing ephemeral environments with GitHub Actions and Qovery

#### Tutorials

- [Deploy Your First Application](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/getting-started/deploy-your-first-application.md): Deploy an application from a Git repository or a container registry to a Kubernetes cluster in your own cloud account, with production and staging environments, from a coding agent, the CLI or the Console.
- [Create a Database](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/getting-started/connect-database.md): Add a database to your environment and connect your application to it with the connection URI and the environment variables Qovery creates.
- [Database Seeding with Lifecycle Jobs](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/others/database-seeding-lifecycle-job.md): Seed a PostgreSQL database from SQL scripts with a Qovery Lifecycle Job, including idempotent, conditional and per-environment seeding.

##### Advanced Tutorials

###### Infrastructure & Security

- [Use AWS IAM Roles with Qovery](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/aws-iam-roles.md): Grant AWS IAM permissions to applications without managing credentials
- [Certificate Management for Multi-Tenant Applications](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/certificate-management-multi-tenant.md): Implement robust SSL/TLS certificate management for multi-tenant SaaS applications
- [Integrate Application Logs to CloudWatch](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/cloudwatch-integration.md): Stream Kubernetes pod logs to AWS CloudWatch for full-text search
- [Deploy a DaemonSet in a Karpenter Context](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/deploy-daemonset-karpenter.md): Schedule a DaemonSet on all Qovery Karpenter node pools: use the Qovery PriorityClass, tolerate the stable and cronjob taints, and skip Fargate nodes.
- [HPA vs KEDA: Choosing an Autoscaling Mode](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/hpa-vs-keda-autoscaling.md): When to scale on CPU and memory with HPA, when to scale on events with KEDA, and how to configure each on Qovery
- [Minimize downtime while upgrading RDS instances](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/upgrading-rds-instance.md): Upgrade an RDS PostgreSQL or MySQL instance with AWS Blue/Green deployments to reduce downtime, then align the database configuration in Qovery.

###### Networking & Access Control

- [Setting Up Cloudflare and Custom Domain on Qovery](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/cloudflare-custom-domain.md): Configure Cloudflare as a domain provider for your Qovery applications
- [How to Setup Rate Limit on Services](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/rate-limiting.md): Configure rate limiting for services using NGINX
- [How to Setup IP and Header-Based Authorization](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/ip-header-authorization.md): Restrict access to a service by combining client IP ranges and an HTTP header, using NGINX snippets on a Qovery-managed cluster.
- [Filter Outbound Traffic with an Egress Proxy](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/egress-filtering-squid-proxy.md): Restrict outbound HTTP(S) traffic for a single application using a Squid forward proxy and Kubernetes NetworkPolicy
- [Isolate Environments with Kubernetes NetworkPolicies](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/isolate-environments-network-policies.md): Block traffic between environments that share a cluster by deploying a NetworkPolicy as a Qovery Helm service
- [Customizing Preview URL with Qovery CLI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/customizing-preview-url-with-qovery-cli.md): Create a custom domain for a service with the Qovery CLI when a new environment is created, get its validation domain, add a CNAME record and redeploy.
- [Expose a Qovery Service on Your Tailnet with Tailscale](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/tailscale-expose-service.md): A step-by-step guide to running the Tailscale Kubernetes Operator as a Qovery Helm service on EKS, and choosing what your tailnet can reach.

###### Development & Deployment

- [How to Write a Dockerfile](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/write-dockerfile.md): Write a Dockerfile and a .dockerignore file for your application, with complete examples for Python Flask, Node.js Express and a multi-stage Go build.
- [Import Environment Variables with the Qovery CLI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/import-env-vars-cli.md): Bulk import environment variables and secrets from a .env file
- [Deploy JupyterHub using Helm](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/deploy-jupyterhub.md): Deploy JupyterHub on Qovery using the official Helm chart
- [Create a Blazingly Fast REST API in Rust (Part 1/2)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/rust-api-part-1.md): Build a performant Twitter clone API with Rust and deploy on Qovery
- [Run a Microservices Monorepo Without Rebuilding Everything](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/guides/advanced-tutorials/microservices-monorepo.md): A practical architecture and rollout playbook for keeping twenty services in one repository while preserving independent builds, deployments, and ownership.

#### Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/troubleshoot/overview.md): Diagnose a failed build or deployment from its logs, then fix common service deployment, runtime and cluster issues on Qovery.

#### Useful Resources

- [FAQ](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/useful-resources/faq.md): Answers to common questions about projects and environments, databases, Git providers, cluster access, Kubernetes upgrades and how Qovery works.
- [Help and Support](https://www.qovery.com/docs/getting-started/useful-resources/help-and-support.md): Get help from the AI Copilot, contact Qovery support through Pylon in the Console or your Slack channel, and read the shared responsibility model.

### Configuration

#### Overview

- [Configuration Overview](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/overview.md): Complete guide to configuring and managing your infrastructure with Qovery

#### Account & Organization

- [User Account](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/user-account.md): Manage your personal account settings and preferences
- [Organization](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization.md): Create, switch and delete Qovery organizations, and manage billing and organization settings. Only the organization owner can delete it.

##### Access & Security

- [Members & RBAC](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/members-rbac.md): Manage organization members and role-based access control
- [SSO (SAML/OIDC)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/sso.md): Configure Single Sign-On with your Identity Provider
- [API Token](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/api-token.md): Manage API tokens for programmatic access to your organization
- [API Policy Token (Preview)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/api-policy-token.md): Give an autonomous agent programmatic access to your organization, constrained by a policy evaluated on every request

#### Clusters & Cloud

- [Clusters](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/clusters.md): Create, update, stop, restart and delete Kubernetes clusters in Qovery, read their statuses and logs, and set up a custom domain with wildcard TLS.
- [Cluster Advanced Settings](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/cluster-advanced-settings.md): Fine-tune your Kubernetes cluster infrastructure with advanced configuration options
- [Connect to Your Cluster](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/connect-to-cluster.md): Run kubectl against your Qovery cluster from the Console shell, the Qovery CLI or the AWS CLI to inspect pods, read logs and debug services.
- [Cloud Credentials](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/cloud-credentials.md): Manage cloud provider credentials for your organization
- [Cloud Provider Resource Tags](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/cloud-provider-resource-tags.md): Default tags Qovery applies to the cloud resources it provisions on AWS, GCP, Azure, and Scaleway

##### AWS EKS

- [AWS EKS Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/eks/overview.md): Deploy on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service with Qovery
- [AWS EKS](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/eks/managed.md): Connect your AWS account and create an EKS cluster managed by Qovery with Karpenter, then tune node pools, check network options and place services.
- [AWS Cluster Preflight Checks](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/eks/preflight-checks.md): Understand the automatic prerequisite validation checks that run before AWS EKS cluster creation
- [AWS EKS Anywhere](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/eks/eks-anywhere.md): Deploy EKS on your own infrastructure with Qovery

##### Google GKE

- [Google GKE Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/gke/overview.md): Deploy on Google Kubernetes Engine with Qovery
- [Qovery-Managed GKE](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/gke/managed.md): Connect your GCP account and create a GKE cluster managed by Qovery, optionally encrypted with your own KMS key, then edit settings and check its network.

##### Azure AKS

- [Azure AKS Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/aks/overview.md): Deploy on Azure Kubernetes Service with Qovery
- [Qovery-Managed AKS](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/aks/managed.md): Connect your Azure account and create an AKS cluster managed by Qovery, then edit its general settings, credentials and mirroring registry.

##### Scaleway Kapsule

- [Scaleway Kapsule Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/scaleway/overview.md): Deploy on Scaleway Kubernetes Kapsule with Qovery
- [Qovery-Managed Scaleway Kapsule](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/scaleway/managed.md): Connect your Scaleway account and create a Kapsule cluster managed by Qovery, then edit its settings, network and static IP for egress traffic.

##### Other Kubernetes

- [Bring Your Own Kubernetes (BYOK)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/byok.md): Connect an EKS, GKE or Kapsule cluster with the Qovery Operator, or try it on local k3s with qovery demo up. Other clusters you run use the Qovery CLI.
- [Supported cluster setups for your own cluster](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/byok-supported-setups.md): Qovery runs on any Kubernetes cluster: the Qovery Operator for EKS, GKE and Kapsule, the Qovery CLI for others. Check version, prerequisites and conflicts.
- [Install Qovery on other Kubernetes clusters with the CLI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/byok-legacy.md): Install Qovery with qovery cluster install on any Kubernetes cluster other than EKS, GKE and Kapsule, such as AKS, k3s, OpenShift or an on-premise cluster.
- [Local Cluster for Development](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/kubernetes/docker.md): Use a local k3s cluster with Docker for development and testing

#### Source Control

- [Git Repository Access](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/git-repository-access.md): Configure Git repository access for your organization

##### Container Registries

- [Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/container-registry.md): Manage container registries for your organization
- [Docker Hub](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/docker-hub.md): Connect Docker Hub to Qovery with an access token to deploy public or private images, and plan for Docker Hub pull rate limits.

###### Cloud Registries

- [AWS ECR](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/aws-ecr.md): Connect Amazon Elastic Container Registry with Qovery
- [GCP Artifact Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/gcp-artifact-registry.md): Connect Google Cloud Artifact Registry with Qovery
- [Azure Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/azure-acr.md): Connect Azure Container Registry (ACR) with Qovery
- [Scaleway Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/scaleway-cr.md): Connect Scaleway Container Registry with Qovery

###### Git-based Registries

- [GitHub Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/github-cr.md): Connect GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) with Qovery
- [GitLab Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/gitlab-cr.md): Connect GitLab Container Registry with Qovery
- [Generic Container Registry](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/container-registries/generic.md): Connect any Docker-compatible container registry with Qovery

##### Helm Repositories

- [Helm Repository](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/helm-repository.md): Manage Helm chart repositories for your organization

#### Projects & Environments

- [Project](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/project.md): Create, edit and delete projects, which group the environments that run the same application and control who can access them.
- [Environment](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/environment.md): Create production, staging, development and preview environments, add services to them, and set deployment rules and preview environments per pull request.

#### Services

##### Workloads

- [Application](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/application.md): Create an application from a Git repository or a container registry, then set its resources, autoscaling, ports, domains, health checks and build settings.
- [Helm Charts](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/helm.md): Deploy a Helm chart from a Git repository or a Helm repository as a Qovery service, override its values, add domains, and auto-deploy charts from Git.

##### Jobs

- [Cron Jobs](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/cronjob.md): Run a container on a schedule with a cron job built from Git or a container registry, set its schedule, restart policy and max duration, or force a run.
- [Lifecycle Jobs](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/lifecycle-job.md): Execute jobs during environment lifecycle events

##### Agent Tasks

- [Agent Tasks](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/overview.md): Configure AI agents that run as jobs on your Qovery infrastructure

###### Examples

- [Incident Analyzer with incident.io](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/incident-analyser.md): Ready-made Agent Task that correlates a firing incident.io incident with recent changes, logs, and metrics
- [Incident Analyzer with Honeybadger](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/incident-analyser-honeybadger.md): Ready-made Agent Task that correlates a firing Honeybadger incident with recent changes, logs, and metrics
- [Build & Deployment Optimizer](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/build-deployment-optimizer.md): Ready-made Agent Task that proposes faster, cheaper build and deployment configurations
- [Jira Coding Agent](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/jira-coding-agent.md): Ready-made Agent Task that picks up a Jira issue and proposes the corresponding code change
- [Linear Coding Agent](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/agent-tasks/linear-coding-agent.md): Ready-made Agent Task that picks up a Linear issue and proposes the corresponding code change

##### Data & Infrastructure

- [Databases](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/database.md): Deploy a managed database from a Blueprint for production, or a container database on your cluster for development, and connect it to your services.
- [Object Storage](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/object-storage.md): Use cloud object storage for persistent data in your applications
- [Terraform](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/terraform.md): Deploy and manage Terraform modules natively on Qovery

##### Blueprints

- [Blueprints](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints.md): Provision managed cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes add-ons, and third-party SaaS resources from Qovery's catalog, no Terraform or Helm required

###### Databases & Caches

- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-elasticache-redis.md): AWS ElastiCache for Redis 7 replication group with TLS and auth token, attached to the Qovery cluster network, with configurable size, topology, backups and maintenance
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Redis (legacy single node)](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-elasticache-redis-node.md): Adopts an existing single-node AWS ElastiCache for Redis cluster created by Qovery native managed Redis. Import only: it cannot create a new cluster. This shape has no auth token and no TLS.
- [Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-elasticache-valkey.md): AWS ElastiCache for Valkey replication group with TLS and auth token, attached to the Qovery cluster network, with configurable size, topology, backups and maintenance
- [Amazon RDS for MySQL](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-rds-mysql.md): AWS RDS MySQL 8.4 instance with configurable size, storage, backups, maintenance, monitoring, and network
- [Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-rds-postgresql.md): AWS RDS PostgreSQL 18 instance with configurable size, storage, backups, maintenance, monitoring, network, and optional read replicas
- [Google Cloud Memorystore for Redis](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/gcp-memorystore-redis.md): GCP Memorystore for Redis 7 instance with configurable tier, memory size, auth, TLS, persistence, maintenance window, and optional read replicas
- [MongoDB Atlas Cluster](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/mongodb-atlas-cluster.md): Provision a MongoDB Atlas dedicated cluster (advanced_cluster) with a database user and IP access list, via the MongoDB Atlas Terraform provider
- [PlanetScale Database](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/planetscale-database.md): Provision a PlanetScale (Vitess/MySQL) database with a production branch and an application password, via the official PlanetScale Terraform provider
- [Redis](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-redis.md): Redis cache via the community groundhog2k Helm chart (official docker.io/redis image)
- [Scaleway Managed PostgreSQL](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/scaleway-managed-postgresql.md): Scaleway Managed Database PostgreSQL instance with configurable node type, storage, backups, and network ACL
- [Scaleway MySQL](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/scaleway-mysql.md): Scaleway Managed Database MySQL instance with configurable node type, storage, backups, and network ACL
- [Timescale Cloud Service](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/timescale-cloud-service.md): Provision a Timescale Cloud (TimescaleDB/Postgres) service with configurable CPU, memory, and HA replicas, via the Timescale Terraform provider

###### Messaging & Streaming

- [Aiven for Apache Kafka](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aiven-kafka.md): Managed Apache Kafka on Aiven (single aiven_kafka service with SASL credentials) via the Aiven Terraform provider
- [Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-amazon-mq-rabbitmq.md): Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ 4 broker over AMQPS, attached to the Qovery cluster network, single node or three-node cluster. Requires mq:* on the deploying IAM role (see README).
- [Amazon MSK](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-msk.md): Amazon MSK Serverless (managed Kafka) with SASL/IAM auth, attached to the Qovery cluster network
- [Confluent Cloud for Apache Kafka](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/confluent-kafka.md): Confluent Cloud Kafka cluster (Basic) with an environment, service account, and client API key, via the Confluent Terraform provider
- [RabbitMQ](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-rabbitmq.md): RabbitMQ message broker via the community groundhog2k Helm chart (official docker.io/rabbitmq image)
- [Redpanda Cloud](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/redpanda-kafka.md): Redpanda Cloud serverless Kafka-compatible cluster via the official Redpanda Terraform provider

###### Storage

- [Amazon S3](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-s3.md): S3 bucket with encryption, versioning, and public-access blocking
- [Scaleway Object Storage](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/scaleway-object-storage.md): Scaleway Object Storage bucket

###### Networking & Edge

- [AWS CloudFront](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-cloudfront.md): AWS CloudFront CDN distribution in front of an HTTP/S origin (ALB, app host, or S3 website), with configurable caching, price class, custom domains, and geo restrictions
- [Cloudflare DNS Zone](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/cloudflare-dns-zone.md): Manage a Cloudflare DNS zone for a domain you already own (with an optional DNS record) via the Cloudflare Terraform provider

###### Compute & Runtime

- [Cloudflare Workers](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/cloudflare-workers.md): Deploy a Cloudflare Worker script (with an optional route) via the Cloudflare Terraform provider
- [Temporal Cloud Namespace](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/temporal-cloud-namespace.md): Provision a Temporal Cloud namespace (regions, retention, client auth) via the Temporal Cloud Terraform provider

###### AI & Analytics

- [AWS Bedrock Access](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/aws-bedrock-access.md): Provision scoped AWS Bedrock access — an IAM policy limited to the models you name, plus an optional IAM user with keys — so an application on any cloud (AWS, Azure, Scaleway or GCP) can call Bedrock models
- [Google BigQuery Dataset](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/bigquery-dataset.md): Provision a Google BigQuery dataset with an optional dedicated service account and key, so an application on any cloud — AWS, Azure, Scaleway or GCP — can query it
- [Snowflake Database](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/snowflake-database.md): Provision a Snowflake database, schema, warehouse and application role, with an optional SERVICE user and generated key pair so an application on any cloud — AWS, Azure, Scaleway or GCP — can connect

###### Observability

- [Datadog](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-datadog.md): Datadog Agent (metrics, logs, optional APM) on Kubernetes via the official Datadog Helm chart
- [Grafana](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-grafana.md): Grafana wired to the cluster's Qovery-managed Prometheus (Thanos), Loki and Alertmanager, with Kubernetes dashboards preloaded
- [New Relic](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-newrelic.md): New Relic Kubernetes monitoring (infrastructure agent, kube-state-metrics, events, optional logs) via the official nri-bundle Helm chart
- [SigNoz](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/blueprints/helm-signoz.md): SigNoz APM (traces, metrics, logs over OpenTelemetry) with the cluster's Qovery-managed Prometheus metrics federated in
- [Service Health Checks](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/service-health-checks.md): Configure liveness and readiness probes to monitor your application health
- [Service Advanced Settings](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/service-advanced-settings.md): Fine-tune your Qovery services with advanced configuration options

#### Deployment & CI/CD

- [Deployment](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/overview.md): Follow how Qovery deploys your services to your cluster, the three ways to trigger a deployment, and where to monitor its progress.
- [Deployment Pipeline](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/pipeline.md): Order service deployments with deployment stages, skip services, and speed up builds and deployments with parallelism and Dockerfile caching.
- [Auto-Deploy](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/auto-deploy.md): Turn on auto-deploy so each Git commit redeploys your service, filter which commits trigger it, and call the Qovery API to deploy new container image tags.

##### Deployment Configuration

- [Deployment Actions](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/actions.md): Deploy, redeploy, stop or restart services and environments, cancel a running deployment, deploy a specific version, and see how actions are queued.
- [Deployment Strategies](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/strategies.md): Choose between RollingUpdate, which replaces pods without downtime and rolls back on failure, and Recreate, which stops old pods before starting new ones.
- [Image Mirroring](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/image-mirroring.md): Qovery copies container images to a registry in your cloud to speed up deployments and scale-ups. See its two modes and how to turn it off on Kapsule.
- [Deployment Rules](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment-rule.md): Automate environment lifecycle management to optimize costs and save time

##### Monitoring Deployments

- [Running and Deployment Statuses](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/statuses.md): Read the running and deployment statuses of environments, services and pods in the Qovery Console, and see how a deployment moves between them.
- [Logs](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/logs.md): Read pre-check, deployment and live service logs in the Qovery Console, filter them by deployment ID, and check how long logs are kept.
- [Deployment History](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/deployment/history.md): See past deployments of an environment or service with their trigger, author, duration and status, and cancel a deployment or open its logs.

##### CI/CD Integrations

- [GitHub Actions](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/ci-cd/github-actions.md): Deploy applications and containers from GitHub Actions with the Qovery CLI, including monorepos, and create, deploy and delete preview environments.
- [GitLab CI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/ci-cd/gitlab-ci.md): Deploy applications and containers from a GitLab CI pipeline with the Qovery CLI, including monorepos, and create, deploy and delete preview environments.
- [CircleCI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/ci-cd/circleci.md): Deploy one or more applications from a CircleCI pipeline with the Qovery CLI, including monorepos, and create, deploy and delete preview environments.
- [Jenkins](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/ci-cd/jenkins.md): Deploy one or more applications from a Jenkins pipeline with the Qovery CLI, including monorepos, and create, deploy and delete preview environments.
- [ArgoCD Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/argocd.md): Monitor and access ArgoCD-managed applications directly from Qovery

#### Environment Variables & Secrets

- [Environment Variables](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/environment-variables.md): Manage environment variables and secrets for your services
- [Doppler](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/secret-managers/doppler.md): Sync secrets from Doppler to your Qovery applications, containers and jobs using a Qovery API token and the Qovery integration in Doppler.

##### Secret Manager Integration

- [Overview](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/secret-managers/secret-manager-access.md): Configure external secrets providers within your Qovery cluster
- [AWS Secrets Manager](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/secret-managers/aws-secrets-manager.md): Connect your Qovery cluster to AWS Secrets Manager using ESO
- [AWS Parameter Store](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/secret-managers/aws-parameter-store.md): Connect your Qovery cluster to AWS Parameter Store using ESO
- [GCP Secret Manager](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/secret-managers/gcp-secret-manager.md): Connect your Qovery cluster to GCP Secret Manager using ESO

#### Observability

- [Qovery Observe](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/observability/qovery-observe.md): Built-in observability for monitoring applications and infrastructure
- [Datadog Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/observability/datadog.md): Deploying Datadog on Qovery: The Complete Guide
- [Kubecost](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/observability/kubecost.md): Monitor and reduce Kubernetes spend with Kubecost

#### Notifications

- [Webhooks](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/webhooks.md): Get notified about deployment events via webhooks
- [Slack Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/slack.md): Get real-time deployment notifications and alerts in Slack
- [Email Integration](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/email.md): Receive real-time alerts via email when your services trigger monitoring conditions

#### Networking & Advanced

##### Networking

- [VPC Peering](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/aws/vpc-peering.md): Peer the VPC of your Qovery cluster with an existing AWS VPC so your applications can reach resources there, such as an RDS database.
- [Use the ECR Pull Through Cache on Your Existing VPC](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/aws/ecr-pull-through-cache-existing-vpc.md): Create the VPC endpoints that keep the image pulls of the ECR pull through cache inside a VPC you manage
- [API Gateway with NGINX](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/api-gateway-nginx.md): Put an NGINX API gateway in front of several Qovery applications, route requests to each one by path, and expose the gateway on a custom domain.

##### Advanced Configuration

- [Labels & Annotations](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/organization/labels-annotations.md): Manage Kubernetes labels and annotations for your organization
- [Disaster Recovery](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/disaster-recovery.md): Best practices for building resilient, reproducible, and tested DR strategies leveraging Qovery's Infrastructure as Code capabilities

##### Infrastructure as Code

- [Infrastructure as Code](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/iac/overview.md): Manage infrastructure through popular IaC frameworks
- [Terraform](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/iac/terraform.md): Run Terraform manifests from your Git repository with a Qovery Lifecycle Job, and pass the Terraform outputs to other services as environment variables.
- [CloudFormation](https://www.qovery.com/docs/configuration/integrations/iac/cloudformation.md): Deploy a CloudFormation template with a Qovery Lifecycle Job to create AWS resources such as databases, Lambda functions or message brokers.

### Terraform Provider

#### Getting Started

- [Terraform Provider](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/overview.md): Manage Qovery resources as code with the Qovery Terraform provider
- [Start a New Project with Terraform or OpenTofu](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/from-scratch.md): From an empty AWS account to an EKS cluster, Postgres and an application in staging and production, all in Terraform or OpenTofu
- [Terraform Exporter](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/exporter.md): Generate the Terraform configuration of an existing Qovery environment, from the Console or with the qovery-terraform agent skill

#### Examples

- [Basic Application](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/basic-application.md): Deploy an application built from a git repository with Terraform
- [Application with Database](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/application-with-database.md): Connect an application to a database with built-in variables
- [Linking Services Together](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/linking-services.md): Use environment variable aliases to connect services using Qovery's built-in variables in Terraform
- [Multi-Environment Setup](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/multi-environment.md): Deploy the same stack to development, staging and production environments
- [Airbyte Deployment](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/airbyte-deployment.md): Complete example deploying Airbyte with Helm, database, and proxy
- [Advanced Patterns](https://www.qovery.com/docs/terraform-provider/advanced-patterns.md): Manage Qovery at scale with Terraform modules, one workspace per environment, remote state, variable files and conditional resources.

### CLI

#### Getting Started

- [Qovery CLI](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/overview.md): Install the Qovery CLI, log in, set a default context and run your first commands from the terminal

#### Commands

- [Commands Overview](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/overview.md): Find the right Qovery CLI command for a task, with the global flags and the full list of commands
- [qovery api](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/api.md): Call any Qovery API endpoint from the terminal with your CLI login, and print the OpenAPI specification
- [qovery application](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/application.md): Deploy, redeploy, restart, stop, clone or delete applications, and manage their domains, variables and secrets
- [qovery audit-log](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/audit-log.md): Export your organization's audit logs for a date range to a CSV file
- [qovery auth](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/auth.md): Log in to Qovery from a browser or a headless session, check your login status and print the access token
- [qovery blueprint](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/blueprint.md): Move a blueprint service, such as an RDS database, to a newer major version from the terminal
- [qovery cluster](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/cluster.md): List, install, deploy, upgrade, stop and lock clusters, download a kubeconfig and open a debug pod
- [qovery completion](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/completion.md): Turn on tab completion for Qovery CLI commands and flags in bash, zsh, fish or PowerShell
- [qovery console](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/console.md): Open the service selected in your CLI context in the Qovery Console in your browser
- [qovery container](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/container.md): Create, deploy, restart, stop or clone container services, and manage their domains, registries, variables and secrets
- [qovery context](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/context.md): Show or set the organization, project, environment and service the CLI targets by default
- [qovery cronjob](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/cronjob.md): Deploy, redeploy, stop, clone or delete cron jobs, and manage their variables and secrets
- [qovery database](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/database.md): List, deploy, redeploy, restart, stop or delete databases, and show their connection credentials
- [qovery demo](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/demo.md): Create a local Kubernetes cluster with Qovery installed to try the platform, then destroy it
- [qovery enterprise-connection](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/enterprise-connection.md): View and update SSO enterprise connections and map identity provider groups to Qovery roles
- [qovery env](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/env.md): Import variables and secrets from a .env file into a service, or turn a Heroku config into a .env file
- [qovery environment](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/environment.md): Deploy, redeploy, stop, cancel, clone or delete environments, print deployment logs, and manage variables, stages and statuses
- [qovery helm](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/helm.md): Deploy, redeploy, stop, clone or delete Helm chart services, and manage their domains, variables and secrets
- [qovery help](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/help.md): Show the usage, subcommands and flags of any Qovery CLI command in the terminal
- [qovery lifecycle](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/lifecycle.md): Deploy, redeploy, stop, clone or delete lifecycle jobs, and manage their variables and secrets
- [qovery list-commands](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/list-commands.md): Print every Qovery CLI command and subcommand with its flags, types and defaults in one list
- [qovery list-pods](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/list-pods.md): List the running pods of a service and the ports each pod exposes
- [qovery log](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/log.md): Stream the logs of an application, container, database or job to your terminal
- [qovery organization](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/organization.md): List the organizations your login or API token can access, with their ID, name and plan
- [qovery port-forward](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/port-forward.md): Forward a local port to a service running on Qovery, such as a database or a private API
- [qovery project](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/project.md): List projects and create, update or delete project-level variables and secrets from the terminal
- [qovery service](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/service.md): List all services of an environment, and deploy one or several services by name whatever their type
- [qovery shell](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/shell.md): Open a shell or run a command in a service container, or in an ephemeral clone pod or debug container
- [qovery status](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/status.md): Print the deployment status of the application or container selected in your CLI context
- [qovery terraform](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/terraform.md): List, plan, apply and delete Terraform services, and manage their state and external secrets
- [qovery token](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/token.md): Generate an API token for CI/CD pipelines, scripts and other non-interactive use of the CLI
- [qovery upgrade](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/upgrade.md): Replace the installed Qovery CLI binary with the latest release in one command
- [qovery version](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/version.md): Print the version of the Qovery CLI installed on your machine
- [qovery webhook](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/commands/webhook.md): List an organization's webhooks and inspect the events each one sent, with response codes

#### Troubleshooting

- [Troubleshooting](https://www.qovery.com/docs/cli/troubleshoot/overview.md): Fix common Qovery CLI errors, such as a broken authentication context or an outdated CLI version
